IGIC Earnings Update and Thoughts on AI:

IGIC generated an ROE of 16.9% and EPS of $0.67, marginally ahead of the $0.66 consensus. Net Premiums earned were up 8.5% YOY, and the combined ratio was 85.7%. Once again, IGI's results were heavily impacted by the Middle East War, which added $8.6 Million in catastrophe losses in the quarter, and roughly $40 Million YTD (almost $1 a share). The stock was down 3% today, likely due to IGI's conservative stance during the call. CEO Waleed Jabsheh acknowledged competition is increasing and that pricing is softening in some lines. IGI has a history of under promising and over delivering, their commentary on each call tends to be cautious, yet each year they generate industry leading results. Even with a headwind from Middle East cat losses, IGI has generated $2.42 in EPS in the trailing four quarters, and I think their India Expansion and new Cipher Cyber Insurance MGA will propel the company back to $3+ in EPS next year. I think < $24 represents an attractive entry.

"The market is never wrong, only opinions are" is one of my favorite quotes. Today, we saw a huge move within tech: Google, Microsoft, Amazon up 5% each, while Nvidia, AI Construction, and Memory dropped. I think the market is sending a message: capex might slow down next year as a result of data center delays. The Democrats scored a definitive win last night with 55-56 senate seats, ~250 house seats, and governorships in data friendly states like Texas and Ohio. Unregulated utilities like Vistra, Talen, and Constellation plunged, and the AI Infrastructure sector dropped 15%. A lot of bulls, whether for AI Infrastructure or even Memory are pointing at forward estimates as evidence that these names are cheaper than ever, but back to the quote, the market simply doesn't care, or is saying that these estimates can be wrong. A delay on new data centers allows hyperscalers to gouge existing prices and pull back on capex, which is very bad news for suppliers like Nvidia, Micron, Hynix, etc. It just takes one "Google announces $xx Billion reduction in 2027 Capex" to send the Memory producers down another 20%.

The options protection from the October 17th piece and the Portfolio review are helping out significantly. WDC is below the Dec 350s, Micron is far below the Dec 1,000 - 1,500 collar, GOOGL is pretty far below the 325 - 390 collar, and IESC and FIX are significantly below the November puts (220s on IESC, and 1500s on FIX). I'm firm on letting each of these positions go at options expiry with the exception of Google (will close out the December puts prior to expiry). My delta adjusted weight within AI Infrastructure has dropped from 10% to 2.5%, and within Memory and Storage from 20% to 7.5%. It's a pretty significant drop, but that's because the options protection is working as intended. Either the Memory guys find their footing and rally back towards December, or they don't and they get cut. I think it's way easier to make money when the trend is on your side, and that this isn't the type of market where you want to be fighting the tape or riding things down to your original cost basis. With this in mind, I'll also be closing out the small SK Square buy from last week tonight.

Looks like IESC and FIX are going to be far below the November put protection, going to let both positions get "put" away in November options expiry unless they rally back above the put levels (1500 for FIX and 220 for IESC). In the pre market, S&P futures up 80 points while Nvidia and the data center construction names are down, I think the market is pricing in higher regulatory scrutiny of AI or a crackdown on new data center builds after this Dem sweep, especially the gov flip in Texas. Either one of these options will cast a shadow over the AI trade for the next two years and serve as a large headwind to the construction trade, so if IESC and FIX can't rally back before November options expiry, I'm ok with letting them go.

My exposure to the overall AI trade is the lowest it's been all year as the options collars kick in, Micron heavily below the 1,000 - 1,500 collar, WDC below the 350 puts, the DRAM collar for Hynix and Samsung is starting to help, and Google is way below the 325 to 390 options spread. On Google, I don't intend on letting it go and will cash in the puts prior to expiry, but on the rest of these trade, the options serve as a stop loss and I'm firm on letting them go if they don't rally back before December. Still feeling massively under the weather, but should be back next week for more regular updates.

Will be spending less time at my desk this week as I unfortunately picked up a nasty cold. Anthropic's updated S1 just came out with Q3 revenue of almost $17 Billion, and the Midterms are tomorrow as well as potential de-escalation in Iran. We get an Iran headline once a day now so I'm used to glossing over it, but with crude down 6% I guess the market is pricing in a small chance that the US and Iran come to a ridiculous sweetheart deal just a day before the Midterms. If we do, would be extremely helpful for the inflation picture, and add some jet fuel to risk-on and the AI trade.

The Kospi closed up 2.2% last night despite 383 Billion Won ($285 Million) of foreigner selling, although this flow was just a quarter of Friday's and was largely offset by Hynix repurchasing $274 Million of stock. Still unfortunate Samsung chose to postpone repurchases until January, but easy to see how Hynix's repurchases have a stabilizing effect on the market, and I think Samsung's will as well once the program is formalized in January. Still sitting in the Memory and Storage names with collars, WDC puts, and the DRAM collar in place with December expiration. The market needs to successfully absorb the Anthropic IPO and Meta and Oracle's inevitable equity raises before fears about the AI trade imploding recede. It's a lot of financing. Until then, I want to have the AI positions protected from catastrophic left-tail risk. One thing I've been keeping an eye on is the divergence between US and Asian names since June, Micron has largely held it together while Hynix and Samsung have gotten slammed, seems like the past few days the differential is starting to close.

For the midterms, betting markets are implying a 72% chance of a Dem Sweep, and I think this has a negative read through to the data center and utility names if it ends up being a landslide. Whether anti data center policies actually materialize is unknown, but even the prospect of a withdrawal of government backing, or tighter scrutiny of new projects will have a chilling impact on buildout names like IESC and FIX, and unregulated utilities like Talen, Vistra, and Constellation, particularly Vistra in Texas. For the time being, I have some November put protection on IESC and FIX until we get through the midterms, and I'm not touching any of the utilities. A goldilocks election scenario would be an extremely small margin for either party, leading to gridlock that ensures nothing drastic is passed.

Market seems off to a good start this week, but I'm not chasing. Lot of unknowns to get through, and I'm waiting to add to existing positions once things finally slow down aside from a little OPY today < 85. Going to pick up everything that was trimmed in July, probably a little more, over the next couple of days. Based on the share price dropping, Q4 GAAP earnings will see a $3 - $4 tailwind from lower employee compensation into the close of the year, bumping Tangible Book Value up to around $80 a share. I'm happy to add just a few dollars above Tangible Book, and if the stock trades below, they likely resume repurchasing shares again as they did in 2024 and 2025.

Talk about whipsaw, a rough week indeed. Hynix, WDC, and Micron were actually up 8%, 6%, and 1% respectively from last Friday, but it doesn't feel like it after the Thursday / Friday rugpull. The Nasdaq briefly entered into correction territory today, and SOXX recorded it's second worst daily move of the year at -8%.

Summary of Trades this week: 
- Sale of GDDY into the close today
- Small 0.25% buy in SK Square at 858k
- Sale of Kioxia
- Dip Buying OPY

I think today was an overreaction to Oppenheimer's earnings, which were solid aside from the impact of the Employee Appreciation Rights. I earmarked a portion of the GDDY cash to add to OPY over the coming days. If the stock continues to trade in the 80s, the value of the OAR's will decline significantly in Q4, which will provide a $3+ tailwind to GAAP EPS. Oppenheimer's business model is lumpy, when capital markets activity is slow they put up $1 - $2 in EPS, and when capital markets activity heats up they post $5+. Importantly, the business is always profitable, and I think at just a small premium to Tangible Book Value of $75, the stock is trading near an attractive entry point to add / initiate a new position. I added several hundred shares today, and will be adding more next week after the Midterm results is digested. For GoDaddy, $116 easily exceeded by initial $110 target. At 15x forward earnings, I just don't find it that compelling. If it were to drop down below $100, would re-enter.

It was painful to cut Kioxia this morning at a whimper of what it was back in June - but the market is not sparing anyone who disappoints. RDDT down 30%, INTC down 29%, I think these days it's "shoot first and ask questions later", and after Kioxia's disappointing guide, I don't want to ride along for whatever happens next, especially given they seemed to be dragging their feet on repurchasing shares.

These days, I think downside protection is more important than ever to manage risk efficiently. The Google Collar, Micron Collar, WDC 350 Puts, and DRAM collar helped blunt a lot of the moves this week, and in Google's case, dodge a total implosion. Having a stop-loss isn't enough - if something really blows and the hyperscalers announce a big pullback in spend, semis could open down 10-15% before the market even opens. I'm still holding all the collars / puts from the October 17th article as protection against this.

To be upfront, I think the AI trade is in a really tough spot right now, probably the worst it's been all year. A lot of the AI guys seem to be in denial of this, or continue to reference bullish equity research price targets, but it's clear the market is sending a message. The market is no longer focused on individual earnings, but rather the AI buildout as a whole. Equities puke at every mention of capex or tapping equity financing by GOOGL and META, and if this continues, its possible the hyperscalers finally cave in and cut or slow capex to reduce the need for financing. I don't think this is base case (if it was we'd be much lower), but you need to have some protection in place if this outcome materializes. For my portfolio, I've been using these collars as lines in the sand on many names. I'm not ready to part ways just yet, but I want to have a clear-cut exit plan. If Micron gets back above 1,000 by December or WDC holds 350, great, but if not, it'll be time to say goodbye and move on.
Closing GDDY here at $116, one of the few bright spots today

Trade Update on Kioxia (Closed) and GoDaddy (Closing Later Today):

Morning gents. Shaping up to be a rough day for the AI affiliated names within the Portfolio. 

Kioxia results last night came in slightly ahead of expectations - EPS of 838 Yen in versus the 816 Consensus and Revenue of 2.48 Trillion in versus the 2.45 Trillion consensus. While this was considered a small beat, the Q3 guide was disappointing. The company is looking for Revenue of 2.5 Trillion and EPS of 854 Yen, figures that are essentially flat to Q2, and way behind Sandisk. The company hedged this disappointing guidance by saying growth would pick up in Q4, so it's possible next quarter's underperformance is a result of timing issues / long-term agreements not yet repricing, but I still don't like it. The AI trade is increasingly driven by growth expectations, every disappointing guide is taken out to the woodshed and punished. In this case, the setup now looks extremely murky - after buying back a lot of stock in the 15,000 - 16,000 range just a few months ago, Kioxia is guiding slower growth, uncertainty past 2027, and switching primarily to dividends - it just doesn't feel right to me.

Kioxia's been a large winner this year, even after the pre-market drop it's up 250% YTD and has doubled since March, but I look to the June highs and think "I wish I sold then". You might have a few positions where this rings true. Whenever I'm in a position I'm displeased with, I ask myself "if I didn't own it would I want to own it now". After Kioxia's guide today, the answer would be no. As a result, I closed my position in the after-hours session just a few moments ago at 12,420. It's a sad ending to a trade that I should have handled much better, but I think these days risk management is more important than ever with the AI names, and you have to find a way to detach yourself from your positioning and view things with a neutral eye rather than anchor to where something was trading in June.

Oppenheimer reported earnings today, with GAAP EPS of $0.47, and adjusted EPS of $1.81. The GAAP figure was heavily impacted by the employee share rights increasing in value in Q3 (the stock rallied from $105 to $118), but with the stock down to $107 currently, this increased compensation expense is likely to reverse in Q4 results. Tangible Book Value increased to $75 a share, and Oppenheimer's wealth management segment rose to record $59.6 Billion in AUM, the weak point in the quarter was the capital markets segment, which swung to a $9 Million pre-tax loss mostly as a result of lower equities underwriting fees. Overall a slightly soft quarter, although I think weakness in biotech and overall capital markets activity will eventually reverse within the next tow quarters, which should get Oppenheimer back to a $3 adjusted eps quarterly run rate. Not really looking to add to the stock in the 100s, my entry point for new buys remains in the $90 - $95 range.

For GoDaddy, I plan on getting rid of the position today either via the $102 put being in the money, or selling the stock if it is above $102. GoDaddy is considered to be a consensus loser among Institutions, and I think the only way it can really break the trend is via good reports. Last night's numbers were solid and there were a few analyst price target upgrades, but I don't think the figures were strong enough to make people say "ok, it isn't a loser any more, we should cover". As a result, I want to avoid owning something that is considered "dead money", and will re-buy closer to the next report.

Lastly, the overall market continues to feel precarious. There is a lot of Iran uncertainty, and there were also several articles that Trump is cancelling this weekend's rally appearances, which could potentially indicate Iran escalation.  Crude is up another $2 this morning. Still have the SPY 740 puts for next week as some cheap insurance, and for the overall AI names, keeping risk tightly under control. GOOGL is protected by the 325 - 390 collar, Micron by the 1000 - 1500 December collar, WDC by the 350 puts, and Hynix and Samsung via the DRAM hedge. It's been a wild year, and it feels like things are going to get even crazier. I think a lot of people are introducing leverage to try and revenge trade back to the June highs on many AI names, I see it the other way, I think it makes sense to keep risk under control and just try and make it through the midterms without taking too much damage.

GoDaddy results out - small beat on revenue of $1.342 Billion versus $1.327 Billion consensus, and EPS of $2.08 versus $1.85 consensus. Will see how the stock reacts tomorrow, have the protection in place and I'm not sure if tonight's beat is enough to placate the market.

Sandisk came in $49.51 versus the $46.36 consensus, and guided to $55 - $57 next quarter versus the $53.35 consensus. The stock is down roughly 2% after hours, but they did return $5 Billion in share repurchases, roughly 80% of net income. As is typical for AI names, was a beat, but probably not enough to impress.

The real downer tonight is Intel. It's not a Portfolio holding (along with Sandisk), but they totally whiffed next quarter's revenue guide, guiding at $15 - $16 Billion versus the $17 Billion street consensus. The earnings results seem to have a read through to the entire AI complex after hours, memory, storage, and Nvidia are down 1-3% after hours. Will have an update on Kioxia in the morning.

Once again, if you don't have a collar on GDDY for earnings I think it's worth considering. Seeing some highly unusual put buys prior to the report, mainly 900 of the 100's and 900 of the 97's that expire tomorrow, very minimal activity for calls.

GoDaddy (Collar) and Kioxia earnings out tonight.

As mentioned last week, GoDaddy is a consensus Institutional loser with high short interest, so I think the reaction tonight will be explosive in either direction. To keep things under control, I put on 102 / 122 collar on the position expiring tomorrow, if you happened to miss that trade the Long 99 Put Short 111 Call collar is currently trading for a 25 cent debit, which caps downside to $5 and upside to $6. Similar to Google, I think it makes sense to have protection in place for highly contentious names. The consensus EPS of $1.85 and revenue of $1.32 Billion for GoDaddy seems well within reach, but I think what is more important is their commentary on customer churn and their new Airo offering, which competes with Wix's Base44. Looking at options flow, there was a large buyer of 650 Friday $99 strike puts, so once again, imperative to have a collar in place to keep downside under control, you don't want to be facing a -15% or -20% move without protection - preserving capital is key.

Sandisk and Kioxia both report earnings tonight. I have a small Kioxia position (1.5%), but I feel ambivalent going into earnings tonight. I favor memory more than I do flash. Part of what has been driving the flash trade is expectations of HBF "High Bandwidth Flash" eventually having a role in KV-Cache offtake and perhaps even inference itself, given a much lower cost relative to High Bandwidth Memory. Over the past couple of months it seems interest in HBF has faded slightly, the companies are working on engineering samples but actual usage isn't projected to begin before 2030, which takes away some right tail upside from Sandisk and Kioxia. Flash is much more challenged by China than memory, Samsung, Hynix's, and Micron's HBM has much higher yields and it's unlikely Chinese manufacturers are able to produce large volumes at attractive prices without cutting edge EUV equipment. Flash, on the other hand, is already under threat as China suppliers such as YMTC ramp up high quality supply, so I think the flash suppliers should trade at or below memory multiples, I'm certainly not willing to own them above 5x earnings.

For Kioxia, I'm expecting a small miss relative to the 816 Yen EPS estimate as the company (in typical Japanese fashion) has a history of guilt over raising prices, and is geared more towards longer term agreements which reprice slowly. I'll be paying attention to whether Sandisk and Kioxia elect to agressively return capital: Kioxia blew its entire cash pile buying back 3% of shares outstanding at 16,000 Yen in August, and Sandisk repurchased 2.8 Million shares last quarter around $1,600. If both names follow through and announce similar capital allocaiton intention I think it'll be viewed as slightly bullish, but if Kioxia declines to launch an additional buyback, or Sandisk turns up light on capital returns, I think it is a bad omen for the memory and storage trade. For Kioxia, I'll also be paying attention to details about a future ADR, Kioxia continues to trade at a large discount to Sandisk despite having the same technology and hardware and sharing manufacturing facilities. A freely interchangable ADR next year should boost the valuation, and provide a nice exit opportunity.

Samsung's call just wrapped up. Their commentary was largely similar to Hynix, the only difference was that Samsung stated HBM was sold out in 2027, whereas Hynix stated their HBM was effectively sold out through 2029. I think a likely explanation is that Samsung is still negotiating pricing (perhaps more aggressively), but aside from that, commentary seemed consistent.

Despite the strong results, I'm disappointed in Samsung's "see you next year" capital allocation. The company finalized a sizeable 30 Trillion dividend of 4,601 (which should provide a nice boost to your IBKR account's if you owned Samsung as of September 30th since the dividend is currently recorded as zero), but on the conference call stated the remaining 2026 shareholder return program of 55 - 75 Trillion Won would be finalized after a board meeting in January.

I think the performance differential between Hynix, Micron, and Samsung over the past few weeks is clear: people want shareholder returns now, not later. Hynix came through last night with an immediate share repurchase program and stable quarterly dividend, and Micron already authorized a $35 Billion buyback before it even reported results. I don't doubt Samsung's pledge to return an additional 55 - 75 Trillion Won, but it's disappointing that the Preferred share repurchase program won't kick in for another 3 month, seems like a huge "own goal" Samsung is scoring on itself. Assuming the 4,601 KRW dividend remains consistent (I actually think it'll increase), Samsung Preferred is paying a 10% annualized yield which is reason enough to stay, so still holding my Preferred shares at 5% weight, but the next couple of months will be bumpy without an immediate repurchase program.

Samsung results out. Company has declared a dividend of 4,601 KRW a share (total of 35 Trillion YTD inclusive of the 15 Trillion previous buyback), with plans of 55 Trillion - 75 Trillion in additional share repurchases and dividends for the rest of the year. Importantly, the company stated it "recognizes growing market interest in the price gap between common and preferred shares, and we are committed to actively considering and adjusting the proportion of preferred shares in our share repurchase and cancellation program based on market conditions". This is excellent news, a share repurchase program specifically going after the discount might help us get to 0.9x, currently shares are just 0.79x. I expect the Preferred shares to continue to outperform on the back of this news, and will be listening to the call for any additional information. Revenue came in at 195 Trillion and Operating Profit at 107.4 Trillion, as previously mentioned in their pre-release October. The earnings call will likely explain the mix of dividends and repurchases for the rest of the year.

Disappointing Google results after hours. Search growth came in at 12% versus the 14% consensus, Google Cloud came in at $30.7 Billion versus the $29 Billion consensus, not high enough to impress. I think their frontier model release earlier today was probably timed to mask these results. The deceleration in search growth is what I am most concerned about, if equity research analysts and investors begin applying a "secular decline" multiple to search, there's a lot of downside. We're likely a long way off from search actually declining, but perception is key and even a 2% miss is enough to alarm everyone.

The GOOGL Long 325 Put short 2x 390 Calls for December collar is providing a lot of downside protection here, my plan is to wait until December options expiration before deciding what to do. I lean towards ultimately cashing in the put then and keeping the shares, but will have to see what the overall market is doing. Glad the protection is in place, feels like these results will leave Google in the penalty box for the rest of the year.

MSFT up slightly after hours, but huge moves down in FTNT and NOW souring the mood in tech. Only thing I am really paying attention to for GOOGL and MSFT during the earnings call is capex commentary, which impacts the memory names. Will have an update later tonight with Samsung's results. Was still a great day despite GOOGL, but I think the bar is a bit high for Memory tonight given Samsung's results are already out and will almost assuredly not be as exciting as Hynix's.

A few Portfolio companies reported strong earnings today, NT Butterfield at $1.58 vs the $1.57 consensus, and Georgia Capital grew NAV a further 15% in the quarter to 5,769 a share. NT Butterfield is going through a transition as it closes the purchase of CIBC Caribbean, so it has temporarily paused share repurchases, but I continue to be impressed by their stable credit quality and capital allocation. Looking to add to my position around $55 a share. The good news continues with Georgia Capital, not only are their private Pharmacy, Hospital, and Insurance subsidiaries paying off, the company continues to aggressively return capital. The CEO launched a fresh $50 Million repurchase program today (2% of shares outstanding), and stated: "Given the continued attractiveness of buybacks at the prevailing discount to NAV, GCAP is extending its existing share buyback programme by an additional US$ 50 million". I think they are essentially saying if they continue to trade around 0.7x NAV, they will aggressively repurchase shares, which is why I think an entry in the 4200 - 4300 range is still attractive for a small position. You can't size CGEO up too much since their is a lot of geopolitical risk (Political Instability and Tension with Russia), but I think at a small weight it can add deep value to your Portfolio.

Later today we have Google, Microsoft, and Samsung reporting. Samsung's earnings have already been released, so what really matters is their commentary and their capital allocation program. I think Samsung is likely to veer in the direction of dividends, which should provide a boost to the Preferred shares who still trade at a 21% discount to the Common Shares. In recent weeks the discount has narrowed significantly, but historically the shares have traded at or above 0.85x. I think a large, stable dividend policy would provide an additional incentive for native Koreans to switch from the Common to the Preferred to get a higher yield. A share repurchase program would also be beneficial, but would likely cover only Common shares, thus not providing a significant benefit to those of us who own the Preferred. What I'm excited to see for Samsung is progress in their foundry business. Over the past couple of years, foundry has been discarded as a third-rate non viable money loser, if Samsung can show us a path to profitability within the segment I think it will be viewed as highly positive, and also be assigned a much higher multiple than Samsung's other businesses. For Google, I am positioned relatively neutral with the 1x 325 - 2x 390 December options trade taking a lot off the table. For Google, it will be interesting to see how much equity they issued during the quarter, whether search is stable, and importantly, results from Google Cloud. I anticipate a beat in Google Cloud, but given how muddy the environment is I'm not sure if that will be enough to sway opinion, hence why I have the options overlay.

Not really doing much else today aside from the small buy in SK Square last night. SK Square reports earnings in mid-November, so it will be interesting to see if they commit to using the Hynix dividend to repurchase some shares. Foreigner buying in the Kospi was mildly positive at +540 Million last night, and Hynix has filed to repurchase 250,000 shares tonight. Not quite their previous 500,000 - 600,000 pace, but better than nothing. Cramer is banging the drums on memory yet again, so naturally I expect to see a near term retracement of some of the move. There is an interest rate decision later this afternoon, I expect most participants to vote for No Hike, but Warsh seems to have a way of sending markets down as he rambles and speaks in poems, not looking forward to it. Personally, I don't believe rate hikes make sense, I think inflation is currently supply side driven (largely energy), and that raising rates to spike the economy and slow things down doesn't solve the underlying causes.

Hynix call is wrapping up. The company remains committed to returning value, and also clarified that the 60 Trillion Won buyback goal for 2026 does not include the 10 Trillion employee share acquisition. This leaves the door open to a smaller repurchase program being announced later this year once the current one completes. The company  also addressed the recent "4F" rumor from China that sent memory names swirling, stating that Hynix believes the current 6F platform with EUV based scaling is still the most efficient, and that the company will transition to a 4F structure once reliability, yield competitiveness, and customer interest justify a product transition. On a side note, seeing consistent Kospi foreigner buying, hopefully stable capital allocation and solid results make memory investable to those outside of the AI trade.

Re-entering an extremely small (0.25%) position in SK Square 402340 at 858k after cutting the name in early October. I think the large cash dividends from Hynix will give SK Square ammunition to start a fresh repurchase program after reporting results next week. As always with Korea, moving very small and slowly, waiting to see if other market participants come to this view and saving capacity to add if things reverse (which they easily could).

SK Hynix released results. The company reported Q3 revenue of 104 Trillion Won and operating profit of 83 Trillion Won, versus consensus of 98 Trillion Won in Revenue and 77 Trillion Won in operating profit. Net Income came in at 40 Trillion and probably reflects some type of currency or Kioxia stake accounting adjustment. Operating margin came in about 1.5% higher than consensus at 79.5%.

The company also announced fresh capital return initiatives: a new 20 Trillion Won repurchase program and a third quarter cash dividend of 14 Trillion Won (20,000 a share). The company additionally pledged to return a total of at least 100 Trillion this year, 60 Trillion in repurchases and 40 Trillion in dividends, which implies an additional 26 Trillion Won in dividends will be declared later this year (36,000 a share).

The earnings call will provide additional detail, but in the press release, the company stated it does not expect the supply demand gap to close until 2030 - clearly, the equities market seems to be saying otherwise so it will be interesting to see how aggressively the company defends this view during the call.

Overall, the results were a solid beat, especially given the strengthening Won as a headwind. Still, I think some foreign investors may be disappointed at the size of the buyback (20 Trillion versus the previous 40 Trillion authorization), so it remains to be seen whether the earnings beat is enough to make up for slightly less impressive capital allocation. It's important to note that half of the new repurchase authorization is to acquire shares for employee compensation, so only 1.2% of shares will be cancelled during the quarter, but on the bright side, the company is clearly following through on returning a minimum of 50% of free cash flow.

There were some rumors last night that Hynix is preparing a 16 Trillion one-time special dividend, and the company promptly released a filing saying nothing had been finalized but a variety of shareholder return measures are being considered and will be published along with earnings tomorrow night. I see this as a slight positive - it'd be great if Hynix could accompany a special dividend with a repurchase program in similar size to the previous program.

The Anthropic S1 was just released, and it remains to be seen how the market will digest the news. From initial reporting, it appears Anthropic generated an adjusted quarterly profit for the first time in Q2. I'm not planning to make many trades today, but I am considering adding a few IESC November at the money puts as protection for the position until earnings - unfortunately the infrastructure names seem to be trading extremely poorly as a whole, and I think the only thing that can reset the narrative for individual infrastructure companies are earnings. IESC's earnings should be out November 20th - 21st - I think IESC will be in the penalty box until then and will get rid of the protection closer to the report. If you aren't involved in the infrastructure names, I think it still makes sense to hold back and wait until there is more clarity - the midterms next week could add more uncertainty if anti-data center candidates win in large numbers. Back to Anthropic, remains to be seen how the market spins the S1, I think news coverage is actually just as important as the numbers in terms of determining initial sentiment this morning.

Earnings Calendar / Market Thoughts / Options Trades:

Huge week for the AI trade and overall earnings, here are the reports I'll be following:

Monday - iM Financial Group (139130 KS)
Tuesday - Seagate, NT Butterfield, Hynix (8 PM)
Wednesday - Interest Rate Decision, Google, Microsoft, Samsung
Thursday - Sandisk, GoDaddy, Kioxia, Amazon
Friday - Oppenheimer (Tentative)

The consensus forecasts for Samsung aren't meaningful as the company has already pre-released earnings. Korean equity analysts are looking for Hynix Revenue of 98 Trillion and EPS of 85,000, I have figures slightly lower at 95 Trillion and EPS of 82,000 mainly due to strengthening FX rates. Frankly, I think a headline miss isn't that surprising or a thesis breaker, the main thing to pay attention to is their commentary on the supply demand gap and capital allocation. Hynix is trading at 3.75x annualized quarterly earnings and Samsung Preferred at 3.30x - multiples that imply we are extremely late in the cycle or that an imminent reduction in capex is about to occur.

In order to get the trade back on track, hyperscalers like Google, Microsoft, and Amazon need to thread the needle by keeping capex stable (higher capex might spook their own investor base and lower capex might imply they don't see attractive returns from AI), and Samsung and Hynix themselves need to assuage investor fears by beginning to return capital. Samsung is likely to go down the dividend route - they have already committed to 90-110 Trillion in cash dividends for CY 2026, and will likely finalize the September 30th dividend in the earnings release, which should provide a nice cash infusion to those of you who already own Samsung Preferred. Hynix, on the other hand, is a wild card. They've guided "at least 50% of cumulative free cash flow from 2025-2027", which implies at least 80 Trillion Won of capital returns this year assuming FCF of 160 Trillion. The company has already returned 40 Trillion via the August - October buyback, but given Hynix's poor governance history, there is a lot that could go wrong here. An uncertain capital return framework, or deferring a further share buyback or dividend into 2027 will clearly be viewed as a red flag and a broad negative for the company and probably tanks the memory trade - it's crucial for Hynix to take its moment in the spotlight to commit to shareholder returns and assure investors it isn't going to blow its record FCF on ramping supply.

It feels like there has never been as much uncertainty in the AI trade as there is now - capex is alarming fixed income investors, and no one really knows when the memory, storage, and even GPU cycle will end. Given the uncertainty, I'm still surprised to see implied volatility in GOOGL, DRAM, and EWY much lower than it was in June, and I think this presents an opportunity to collar positions and purchase puts to eliminate significant downside risk, while still leaving the door open to 20-30% price appreciation if "everything works out".

As mentioned in last weekend's piece, I put on long 1x December $325 GOOGL put short 2x December $390 call options overlay, which caps near-term downside risk while still allowing a lot of upside. If you happened to miss that trade, I think a similar variant is the long 1x December $300 put short 2x December $370 call, which costs about $1.40 (less than 0.4% of the current Google price), and limits downside to roughly 6%. Of course, if Google surges above $420 by year end the $370 calls will come back to bite and turn the trade negative, but right now I'm more concerned about downside risk, and happy to trade away right-tail upside in exchange for immediate downside protection. For DRAM, I have a 1/1 collar, long December $40 puts and short December $65 calls for about $1.00 - this caps memory downside risk to about 15%, while leaving about 39% upside if we return to June highs.

For GoDaddy, I will be putting on a Short $122 Call Long $102 Put for October 30th expiration for a small credit. GoDaddy is a heavy consensus short going into earnings, but I also think GoDaddy's capex light nature and the first major quarter of growth in a while might entice investors back into the fold. Given the stock is up nicely since entry but also a battleground name, I'm happy to leave $10 of upside while capping downside to the cost basis, and have also trimmed the position by a third to lock in some profits.

This will be an action packed two weeks: AI earnings, midterms, and the interest rate decision (I don't see a hike). In general I think trading options is a losing endeavor, but in select instances I think they can be helpful in defining risk-to-reward during periods of uncertainty. Will have updates on earnings as they are released.

A lot of whipsaw this week - memory and storage names actually finished slightly up, while SOXX dropped another 3%. Certainly didn't feel like it given the dramatic moves.

GoDaddy set a fresh high (will collar it prior to earnings next week), and CUBI set an all time high after reporting record results! Haven't seen much equity research come out yet, but I think a lot of upgrades are in the works - CUBI is still my top position within banks, and I think time is on our side - as the steady, positive results continue, I think the bank will eventually trade around 10x - 11x EPS in line with peers (frankly, I think it should trade at a premium given the track record).

This week's pain points were mainly IESC and FIX and I continue to keep a close eye on both. FIX is protected by the 1500 Strike November Puts, and I'm more worried about IESC. On my terminal, I've spotted a consistent 25k share a day seller who began on the 13th and has continued to sell each day since - I think IESC is a relatively thinly traded stock, and I'm not looking to bottom fish until the selling pressure ceases. I think some of the recent weakness in the Cooling / Communications / Power names has also come from Nvidia's recent "DSX POD" announcement from Wednesday. To speed up site readiness, Nvidia has now designed Modular Pods that have a lot of cooling and wiring already built-in at the factory level, reducing the amount of on-site work needed to bring the GPUs online. I think this pod design is unlikely to take too much business away from names like Comfort Systems and IESC since most clients and hyperscalers have their own technology / design, but a few years down the line it could take away small chunk of their business. For now, sitting tight on both, and still waiting for things to stabilize before adding more.

Next week is really critical, Amazon, Google, and Microsoft reporting, and more importantly, Samsung and SK Hynix. I remain short term bearish on Google and have the 1x 325 Put Short 2x 390 Call December options combination in place on to minimize risk - I think that as long as people are fearful of an eventual Meta equity raise, GOOGL will continue to trade weakly. Too much capex spooks investors, and too little seems like a sign demand is cooling. It just feels like a "hard to please" setup going into the report. I like the 1x / 2x options combination as I'm more worried about downside risk than upside risk, if Google is anywhere close to 390 (or even above) by December, I really wouldn't mind. If you missed the original combo, you could put on a long December 300 Put Short 2x December 370 Call combo for around 1.50.

Hynix reports Tuesday evening and Samsung reports Wednesday evening. I think it's really up to them to save the AI trade by announcing large buybacks. At a recent event Jensen Huang said the AI buildout's primary constraint is capital, and I think this also applies to the AI trade itself. Right now it feels like a lot of people are on their last legs, there isn't much of a marginal buyer for AI related equities, and that things could easily spiral out of control if panic sets in. Hynix and Samsung are set to rake in more than $100 Billion this quarter, and I think if they chose to sit on this cash rather than distribute it, the market really won't like it.

There's no way to know what they will announce without being an insider - but I do see some positive tea leaves. Recently, Hynix hired bankers for a potential IPO of its Solidigm NAND subsidiary (something institutional investors didn't want to see), and Korea's finance ministry immediately announced they were looking into whether an IPO would violate the country's new dual-listing restriction put into place to protect investors. Hynix promptly placed the IPO on hold.

I think Korean authorities are under a lot of pressure, the market is down 45% from its June peak, opposition lawmakers are investigating why the National Pension Service chose to not rebalance (to sell) Korean equities, and I think there is political pressure to have the market bleeding stop. I think the only real way to do this is via Hynix and Samsung announcing large shareholder return policies. It's an uncomfortable, binary setup ahead of us. Unlike other areas of the Portfolio, like CUBI, where we know there is good management and we are simply making a bet on the valuation, with Hynix and Samsung there is a giant question mark surrounding management quality. It seems obvious they should be returning capital, but they could easily overshadow great results by saying something evasive regarding capital allocation.

In any case, it's been a really long week. Enjoy the weekend, there's another long week ahead of us.

Even after the recent drop, it's still a total return of 131% since the "One Repurchase at a Time" article from August 14, 2025. In other news, 9478 is bumbling around the 500 level - and I'm happy to see that. Their initial repurchase report will be posted at the end of the month, will have an update on it once it comes out to see what levels they are active, and use that to our advantage.

Brutal day for AI related positions.

Western Digital came in at $4.64 in EPS vs the $4.10 consensus and $3.85 to $4.15 guidance, and guided Q4 to $5.60 to $6.00. During the call, the management team was repeatedly pressed by analysts if they'd increase unit capacity as a hypothetical response to Toshiba, and they responded "no". Near-term byte shipments are expected to ramp up and exceed the guided 25% level by 2027 Q2, the CFO commented that over the next 4-6 quarters the rate of price increases was expected to accelerate, and that the company has demand visibility from its top customers to 2030. Despite the strong results and a guide 20% above consensus, the stock is down 5% after hours. I think it's hard to try and pinpoint a reason to explain every move - these days it feels like AI related names are getting taken to the woodshed despite great results, and I think the overall reason behind it is that the market is increasingly pricing the music to stop in 2027: capex cuts. This type of fear is extremely hard to dispell, and unfortunately I think no matter how strong results are, the market simply won't react well until this level of fear receeds.

One of the reasons I have been collaring and adding put protection is it buys time, and I think time is what the market needs to climb the current wall of worry. Ultimately, I think Anthropic's full financials and roadshow over the next month will serve as a critical juncture - either the market gets over extreme fear and Portfolio names like WDC, Samsung Preferred, and Hynix re-rate to more attractive valuations, or I think panic spirals out of control, everything drops a bunch more, and the puts eliminate that downside risk and automatically close positions out in December. It's the same approach I took with Entravision and Powell Industries earlier this year, and the WDC December 350 Puts are my line in the sand.

It was a similar story with Comfort Systems today. EPS came in at $13.91, 9% above the $12.72 consensus, backlog surged another 26% in the quarter from $14.04 Billion to $17.81 Billion (versus consensus of $14.4 Billion). I think the company is setting the stage for $60+ in EPS in 2027. The conference call is tomorrow, but after hours the stock is reacting poorly and down a further 6%. Similar to WDC, I think solid results are being overshadowed by fear as everyone questions the AI buildout. I have the stock paired with November $1,500 strike puts, although closer to the expiration I will close them out and just hold the stock without protection then.

Customers Bank reported excellent earnings of $2.27 (a record) versus the $2.14 consensus. Importantly, credit quaity was extremely stable and the bank brought in another $300 Million in zero cost deposits from its new banking teams. I think we are finally beginning to see the CUBI growth story play out - the company has spent the last two years cutting down on overhead, investing in AI initiatives, and hiring "earners" from rival banks to bring in new deposits. This has skewed CUBI's EPS to the downside in the near term as new hires and AI integration come with significant onboarding expenses and don't begin to yield profits immediately. These dual efforts are finally yielding dividends, as CUBI's average assets per employee have increased 11% this year, revenue per employee 13%, and pre-tax profit per employee 34%. In addition to strong deposit growth from CUBI's proprietary CUBIX platform (mostly driven by new mortgage finance and real estate customers), CUBI was also active on the capital management front, repurchasing about $35 Million of stock during the quarter. I'm very pleased with the results.

OP Bancorp also reported results, EPS of $0.52 versus the $0.49 consensus. OP did see a slight deterioration in credit quality, but the bank has historically navigated this well, and I think OP is well provisioned for any further credit weakness. OP Bancorp is a lower conviction trade for me than Customers since I think a growth story is much more powerful than value within banks, but as long as the company stays on track for $2 in EPS a year, I am happy to hold it at 7.5x earnings, especially as it serves as a counterweight to the AI names.

It's been a really rough stretch since mid-September, and while I wish I could take a strong stance on AI, I'm torn, just as the market is, and perhaps you are. On one hand Samsung Pref < 2.5x 2027 earnings, Hynix < 3x 2027, and WDC < 14x 2027 seem far too cheap, but on the other hand its clear the market is getting close to panicking about about AI spend, and these concerns shouldn't be ignored - there has to be a reason behind them. Every headline relating to Anthropic's IPO or Coreweave's debt is powerful enough to send anything AI affiliated down 2%, so at this point valuations are based off sentiment and not fundamentals, which makes it difficult to pull the trigger on adding any more exposure. The collars mentioned in the weekend piece and the last Portfolio review buy some time and protect downside, ultimately I think it's up to Samsung / Hynix to save the AI trade by announcing large, supportive, capital return programs next week.

On a side note, it's important to put things into perspective and see that under the hood, the market is pretty stable outside of the AI trade. VTV (Value ETF) is just a few bps away from an all time high, and equal weighted S&P is up 5% in October. AI positions are 20% of my Portfolio but seem to cause 90% of the pain, and I think the same goes for the broader market as a whole. The past couple of days have shown how diversification across value is helpful, hopefully banks, insurers, and even GoDaddy continue to chugg higher.

Earnings Results / Setups for 9478, WDC, FIX, CUBI, and Covering AXP Short:

9478 - SE Holdings and Incubations reported another impressive quarter. Tangible Book Value per share grew from 785 Yen to 830 Yen (far exceeding my 795 Yen estimate), amidst a very difficult market in Q3. Like clockwork, the company has announced a fresh repurchase program for up to 400,000 shares or 160 Million Yen until December 18th, which at current prices implies about 300,000 shares, another 2% of the company. I see SE Holdings and Incubations as almost an inverse Microstrategy - rather than constantly diluting shareholders, because it trades so cheaply, it continues repurchasing its own shares with drives Tangible Book Value even higher. When I first mentioned the company last August it was 320 Yen with Tangible Book of 570, ironically today it is trading at almost the same discount simply because it has done so well growing book. I'm moving up my adding range from < 500 to < 520, I think the repurchase program helps tilt the odds in our favor as the company takes out another huge chunk.

Even Meta's report yesterday was much stronger than expected, but the stock has tanked as the filings show they spoke to Moelis about potentially raising hundreds of Billions in the coming years.

While WDC and FIX certainly aren't raising new capital, I think the ripple effect is getting through to them. No matter how much AI related names seem to beat by - the market punishes them.

The consensus for WDC is $4.10 against guidance of $4.00 - I think WDC can easily come in $4.15 - $4.25, but I'm not sure even $4.25 is enough to be considered a beat. People are obviously questioning the sustainability of the AI buildout, and I think all the infrastructure names are getting pounded down into teens multiples until people feel more comfortable. I'm holding the shares against some $1,500 Strike November puts, not trying to catch a falling knife here. CUBI is reporting earnings today, and I think the $2.14 consensus is well within reach, I'm looking for $2.20+. The stock is up $3 in the past few days as people try to jockey in right before earnings, which does make the setup more difficult as rally before earnings is never good. I expect them to move 2026 guidance slightly higher, and perhaps hint at higher 2027 guidance as well.

Overall, still trying to be defensive in my positioning with the DRAM collar, GOOGL collar, and WDC / FIX puts. I think we are at a critical juncture: the articles on credit default swaps for Meta and Coreweave have spun everyone into a tizzy, and I think its clear that in the short-term, people are extremely bearish on semis and anything AI related - so the collars and options help protect against near-term downside without closing the trades. Lastly, AXP is also reporting tomorrow, I think the stock is overvalued, but it fits the mold of quality and capital returns, which seems to be faring well in this market so I finally covered the short.

Hynix's buyback will be fully expended tonight. The company has filed to repurchase 472,080 shares, which means there will be no additional buyback support from Thursday's session onwards to earnings next week. Given where the stock is trading and the analyst research I've read, the market expects them to announce a fresh repurchase program next week. This seems extremely sensible but also presents a risk: if Hynix equivocates on capital returns or says something ambiguous like "we may consider future initiatives at a later time", I think the market will be spooked no matter how impressive results are. At this point, I think they almost have to repurchase - political pressure is mounting, the government financial services regulator is moving to block the IPO of Solidigm, and members of the National Assembly are investigating Korea's pension over rebalancing concerns - the President needs to get the market going to avoid his approval tanking, and given how corrupt the chaebols are in general, I'd guess he probably told them they have to stabilize the market.

In more positive news, A Plus Asset Advisors (244920) finally followed through on its promise to publish a Korea "Value Up" plan. Their plan was extremely comprehensive, with a near-term goal to boost ROE from 13% to 15%+, as well as a steady increase in the payout ratio from 25% in 2026, to 30% in 2027, and 30%+ in 2028. This is exactly what I wanted to see - I think A Plus is one of the cheapest insurance brokerages out there, and the question isn't really a matter of valuation, but rather, can we count on them to return earnings?

In this case, I think it's a clear yes. They've already made huge strides in putting shareholders first, their 20% activist owner Align Partners continues to keep them on a short leash, and last night the company announced a fresh 3.5 Billion Won buyback for an additional 1.2% shares outstanding, showing the value up plan isn't merely lip service.

One of the reasons I cut the Japanese Bank positions in half was so that I could have more room for the new Korean value names, I think the setup in Korean financials is similar to that of Japanese Banks in 2024: huge share repurchase programs, a sudden focus on capital efficiency, and activist attention. I will be adding to my A Plus Position tonight, and am also looking forward to iM Financial Group's report later this month. Both names are down roughly 10% since entry but I see this as a buying opportunity, particularly with supportive share repurchases being announced.

Trade update on IFOS and thoughts on MREITs:

Closing out the IFOS position today for a 30% loss. This one really stings, and it pains me that it dribbled from a +30% gain to -30%. Unfortunately, I think the Hormuz situation is unlikely to resolve anytime soon and that Iran wants to inflict maximum pain on Oil and US Markets going into the midterms, which means the price of Itafos's input, Sulphur, is unlikely to come down anytime soon. Of course, this also bodes very poorly for the overall market, which is why I have paused dip-buying and am sitting on the 20% cash pile for now. I think Itafos is a well-run company that found itself in the wrong spot at the wrong time, and once there is progress in the Middle East I will buy back in quickly, but for now, 30% is max pain where I need to draw the line and cut losses.

Additionally, I'm paying close attention to the MREIT sector as a warning sign for the overall market. Recently there have been plenty of "value" pitches for MREITs trading at the largest-discount since COVID, but I think caution is warranted here and that it makes sense to stay away. One of the most well-known MREITs, Arbor Realty Trust, is flashing an extreme warning signal - their senior bonds are down nearly 20% in the last month and now have a Yield to Maturity of 20-25%. I don't like to be an alarmist, but if the Fixed Income guys think Arbor's debt should yield 20%+ from a 2028 maturity, it's clear something is very wrong. There are plenty of "higher-tier" MREITs like AGNC and NLY that routinely outperform peers, but as long as someone like Arbor is in deep distress, it think it makes sense to stay away from the sector until things stabilize.

JPM and C are kicking off earnings season tomorrow.

In AI news, Meta released their latest model today, which according to the benchmarks is just a little bit behind Anthropic's Opus 5.5

I think it is a great release from them, and also begs the question: if everyone is at the frontier, is anyone at the frontier?

I don't want to pop champagne for Google just yet, but it feels like Meta and Google have essentially jumped from last place to within a hair of Anthropic and OpenAI, largely by spending huge amounts on capex and harnessing massive amounts of internal data. The whole allure of Anthropic and OpenAI isn't their infrastructure or reach, it's simply their lead in model intelligence. I think if Google and Meta (who already have tremendous infrastructure in place and hundreds of millions of users) are just months behind OpenAI and Anthropic, their startup values are questionable. The way I see it is why risk investing in a 2 Trillion valuation for OpenAI or Anthropic when you could get an index level multiple for Meta or Google?

The AI bears are quickly jumping on this train of thought to declare the AI trade dead, but I think there is a middle ground here.

As much as it feels like it, the AI trade isn't dependent on OpenAI or Anthropic reigning supreme. The $4 Trillion combined valuation they seem to think they are worth is a "paper figure", only $300 Billion has actually been invested, and if both companies ultimately don't work out and lose to Google, Meta, or Chinese Open Source models, AI progress will continue to move forward. Historically, there is a lot of precedent for first-to-act companies with new technology falling behind only for the underlying technological trend to continue after their reign. BlackBerry once had more than 50% smartphone share, and is now a small cap that makes auto software and cybersecurity products. Yahoo and AOL dominated the web, only to become forgettable archives that are passed around PE portfolio's like a hot potato. My point is that the leader of a trend being challenged or falling behind peers isn't necessarily indicative of the trend being over, and if anything, I think the fact that Google and Meta are rapidly catching up is a sign that their massive capex is yielding results.

As for the overall AI trade, still expecting a very challenging two weeks given the absence of share repurchase support, frontier lab jitters, and no real earnings announcements that could turn around the trend until Hynix and Samsung report on the 29th and 30th. The MU 1000 / 1500 collar has taken a lot of risk off the table, so I have some extra firepower I am looking to put to work. Tonight, I have orders to add 25 bps to Samsung Pref < 185k, and 25 bps to re-enter SK Square < 900k. These order sizes may seem small, but given how difficult it is to time these instruments, I think it makes sense to move slowly and spread your order over multiple sessions going into earnings, if you find the setup attractive.

The reason for the collapse was that the report mentions $50 Billion in ARR for OpenAI in September, a step down from $70 Billion which was leaked last week.

There's more to the story here, Anthropic reports revenue on a gross basis, which means that money spent on Claude via Microsoft / Google / Amazon API is counted as ARR without deducting the partner's share. OpenAI, on the other hand, reports revenue on a net basis. It appears investors mistakenly took OpenAI's previous figures and grossed them up by adding back partner revenue, which has led to a discrepancy in the numbers last week and what OpenAI reported today.

The knee-jerk plunge highlights how crowded the semis trade is and that a lot of people are short banks and insurers to finance their Semis exposure (which is why I like having banking and insurance exposure, in addition to the very inexpensive valuations). A lot of bears point to the circular nature of AI as evidence that it is a bubble, and I think they have a good point. Without Nvidia backing new neoclouds, or Broadcom or AMD financing chip sales, overall revenue growth would be much lower and new transactions could shrivel up. The guys who are downstream like Hynix, Samsung, Kioxia, Sandisk, Western Digital, Seagate, and Micron are all raking in hundreds of billions in cash, and given how sentiment is souring and debt is getting expensive, they could unleash a new wave of liquidity by simply paying out that cash via repurchases and dividends to shareholders. Almost all of the shareholder base is AI guys (very few value guys), and large cash returns would breathe new life into people's willingness to finance AI. Micron earnings came in at $33.42, beating the $31.83 consensus, and the guide for next quarter is $38.15 plus or minus $1.00, about 6% ahead of the $36 consensus.

Several important things to note during the call.

35% of volume is now covered by SCA's (+15% from last quarter), capex for 2027 will be higher (exact figure not provided), and the company "has no line of sight to when the supply and demand imbalance will close". Sanjay Mehrotra, the CEO, also mentioned Micron is now getting interest in SCAs up to 2031, and that margins are expected to continue improving sequentially.

The stock reacted negatively when Micron's CFO stated "100% of excess cash will be returned", but that Micron was still building towards a "target cash" level that would be reached at the end of Q1 (next quarter), which many took as a sign that Micron didn't like the valuation or wants to drag its feet on returning cash. I wouldn't put too much weight on this, I think Micron is trying to manage expectations and doesn't want to commit to large repurchases only to get front run by the market before they are actually able to repurchase stock.

Overall it was a solid quarter and confirmed the memory shortage is likely to last much longer than initially expected, but I'm not sure the numbers will be enough to be considered a "beat" by the market at the open tomorrow. I much prefer Samsung Preferred and, to a lesser extent, Hynix for memory exposure, and am looking forward to their earnings calls later this month, as well as confirmation from Samsung on its dividend policy.

Also important to note, right after the close Google published preliminary benchmarks for its new Gemini 4 Argon model, which seems on par with Anthropic's Opus 5.5, and OpenAI's Astra 6. Despite being primarily an Anthropic user myself, I'm skeptical of the frontier lab business model. If anything, I think distribution and customer use case matter almost as much, if not more, than a model's actually capabilities, and I think of all the frontier labs, Google has the data, data centers, and use cases to make things work. No doubt, they have their own Agentic offering in the works, and I'm sure we'll see it come out by the end of the year.

Note on Micron earnings and Regional Banks:

Micron is set to report after the close today. Consensus is $31.83 in Adjusted EPS relative to the $30 - $32 management guide, but it's also important to note that last quarter Micron came in at $24.97 against consensus of $20.49 and a management guide of $18.75 - $19.55. Due to Micron's history of beating estimates, the bar is undoubtedly high and I think Micron needs to come in around $33 for the results to be appreciated by markets.

Many people expect a similar Q3 beat, but I think this would be a mistake - management has stated they've seen a "meaningful moderation" in the rate of price increases in Q4. DRAM ASP is expected to be +15% quarter over quarter, and NAND ASP is expected to be +18%, versus Q3's +60% jump in DRAM ASP and +80% jump in NAND ASP, with this in mind, it's clear pricing is improving but slowing, which is why a Q3 level beat is unlikely to repeat itself.

More important than the headline figure, however, is management's commentary on the state of the market, SCA (Strategic Customer Agreements) pricing, and their intention on capital allocation once the CHIPS ACT Moratorium on share repurchases expires two months from now.

As of the last call, it was disclosed roughly 20% of DRAM volume was covered under SCAs, for Q4 I'm expecting them to mention at least 30% is covered by SCAs, if not more. Additionally, I'll be eyeing the capex figure, a large step up from the $40 Billion floor might spark concerns about oversupply or undisciplined pricing. Lastly, will be focusing on days of inventory, it was mentioned in June they had less than 4 months of supply on hand (even less for DRAM), and I think a positive update on there being almost no supply left could feed the bull narrative of the cycle continuing.

I do own a little Micron that I've capped between 1,000 and 1,450 for the rest of the year via options, but I think there is substantially more upside available in Samsung Preferred and Hynix.

Important update to the Blackjack 21: Trade Exit in Ategrity Specialty ASIC (+39%)

In preparation for next week's Portfolio review piece, I've been going through the holdings list one by one. One of the questions I always ask myself is "would I buy at this price if I didn't already own it?" It's not a strict rule and of course you can have some leeway for winners that run, but it's a great gut-check for identifying names that have already played out that you don't have much conviction to, but haven't realized it yet.

Ategrity Specialty was originally a pair trade, the Long Leg against short Kinsale Capital Group (KNSL). At position entry, Ategrity was trading under 10x normalized earnings with a 25% annual growth tailwind, insider buying, and a freshly announced repurchase program. Since December, the stock is up nearly 40% while it's loftily valued peer, Kinsale Capital, is down 16%, and the broader insurance benchmark is exactly flat, an excellent return.

The reason for the sale is simple: E&S (Excess and Surplus) insurance growth, which is Ategrity's and Kinsale's specialty, has slowed significantly. Monthly stamping data from State Regulators has shown the pace of E&S Growth decelerating in May, June, and July (with a respite in August), and while I expect Ategrity to continue growing 20-25% ahead of peers, a broader industry headwind makes it a much more difficult setup.

At roughly 15x normalized earnings (a good chunk of Ategrity's income comes from investments in utility and mid cap hedge funds), and overall 2026 YTD E&S growth coming in around 3% versus 15% in 2025, I think it's time to lock in a big winner here and keep the cash for more attractive opportunities. Plenty of other names in the Portfolio like  International General Insurance (9-10x forward earnings), Hyundai Green Food (5x forward earnings), or iM Financial Group (4.5x forward earnings, 0.45x Tangible Book Value), are trading at much more palatable multiples and actively repurchasing shares. I'd much rather allocate capital to them than hold ASIC at a relatively high forward multiple with high industry uncertainty, ASIC simply isn't a value setup anymore.

With the removal of ASIC, the Blackjack 21 is down to just 15 members, but that's ok with me - unlike big tech or cult-level quality where you can probably hold forever and be alright, I think there is a time and place for insurance and banks and that it pays to be selective. When at attractive levels you can really buy big, and when names like HRTG, CBL, SNEX, WSBF, and now, ASIC, have had their run 30-100% runs, it's ok to convert that gain into cash and wait for more attractive setups rather than to try to hold forever. To be clear, I'm not bearish on ASIC (like I am mildly on CBL), I simply think the thesis has played out and that the risk adjusted return here probably isn't great going forward. I will be on the lookout for new, more attractive trades.

Morning gents. Rates alarmingly continue to march higher, and there was also a lot of concern over the weekend regarding regional banks and the potential for AI agents like Muse to "sweep" cash into higher yield savings accounts.

Ironically, you don't even need an "AI Agent" to do this. Many banks like Ally, Mercury, even Fidelity have high yield money market accounts you can "link" to checking accounts to auto sweep a certain amount, so you can maintain enough cash to write checks and pay your bills while leaving the rest earning a decent yield. So do I think AI agents will cause a bank run? No shot. But do I think it could impact the banking industry somewhat? Yes.

Regional banking is a cutthroat industry, most of the Portfolio holdings like OP Bancorp or Customer's offer highly competitive yields to retail clients, while larger US Institutions like JPM, Wells Fargo, and Citi enjoy huge chunks of retail deposits they pay close to 0% on. If anyone is going to be hurt by "tech enabled" people sweeping cash to high yielding accounts, it's someone like JPM, not a sleepy regional bank.

As a result, to hedge against other Portfolio holdings, I've put on a small 0.5% short in JPM here at $341, with a stop at $350 and looking to take profits at $335.

Another name I am paying attention to on the short side is Uber.

About a year ago, I posted a small piece of news on one of Uber's upstart competitors, Empower, that received a very negative response from Uber bulls on Twitter. Empower is a "bootleg" taxi app, unlike regulated peers like Uber and Lyft, Empower takes no cut of rideshare fees and simply runs a subscription-based app for Taxi Drivers to secure customers (they use this to argue Rideshare regulations are not applicable to them).

While local governments have lashed out, Empower has continued on and is rapidly gaining share in major cities like Miami and New York. The price differential is astounding, rides in New York might be just $30-$40 on Empower versus $70-$90 on Uber during surge pricing, and drivers I ride with are increasingly switching over.

I think this caps near-term upside in the stock, so I've sold Uber 85 Strike January Calls for $1.40. The trade weight is 0.50% on a notional basis, that is I rather than putting 0.50% into short shares, I took the share position and sold a corresponding amount of calls instead. Options selling and shorting is a high risk activity, which is why I sized both of these trades at a 0.50% weight (0.50% JPM Shares, 0.50% UBER Notional translated into calls).

Other names that are "Muse Disrupted" like Intuit, Expedia, and Booking seem weak, but I think the downside is now reflected so I have no strong opinion on them.

Lastly, there is a "special announcement" from President Trump today at 2 PM. My guesses are that it is either AI related due to his meeting with Dario Amodei last night, or potential news on an Iranian plot given recent arrests near an RAF base this weekend, which would probably be bad for bonds and the market and spike oil prices. We'll have to stay tuned.

If short-term interest rates continue to rise, this is very bad news for them especially given most are up 30-50% over the last year. None of them are trading anywhere close to what I'd call "value levels", and if anything I think the setup for names like CBL leans to the downside.

As for the remaining financials holdings that haven't been sold, IGIC, CBNA, OPY, MRX, and ASIC are clear beneficiaries of rising rates, and CUBI and OPBK are slight beneficiaries.

International General Insurance and Ategrity Specialty have short-duration Portfolios and significant cash left in Money-Market funds that can immediately benefit from rising yields, and Chain Bridge, Oppenheimer, and Marex all retain significant client cash close to 0% that will generate higher Net Interest Income. Customers Bank and OP Bancorp similarly have shorter-duration loan books and less CRE exposure than peers. Kaspi is sensitive to Kazakh interest rates, but to be upfront, I really don't have an opinion.

Right now, I think a lot of people aren't taking the move in yields seriously, but if a higher-rate environment persists (which I think it will), you certainly want to steer clear of "rates up" victims and be selective with your positioning. Over the next couple of months I expect financials "rates up" beneficiaries to significantly outperform those who are hurt by rising yields, as people take these concerns more seriously, I think they will slowly filter out of the rates down names, and increase exposure to rate neutral and rates up beneficiaries.

The thesis for Godaddy is pretty simple: it's a melting ice-cube that isn't actually melting. There's a lot of concern about competition, Cloudflare is offering domains at just a few cents above cost (versus Godaddy who might sell a .com domain for $22.99 when it costs them $10), and Wix has a website creation tool, Base44, that is rapidly attracting customers. The market has been highly concerned over these developments challenging future growth, but I think Godaddy is trading at a level where it actually doesn't matter that much.

Godaddy is trading around 11.5x 2027 GAAP earnings with sizeable repurchase activity, and no meaningful debt maturities until 2029. It's debt is trading at a minimal spread to treasuries, so bond investors seem highly content and I don't think Godaddy will have any problems refinancing. Market concerns about competition heating up make sense, but I think investors aren't realizing how "lethargic" Godaddy's client base actually is.

People who have parked or owned domain names for decades don't actually care if a competitor could save them $5, or even $10 a year.

The domains they park represent dreams of a future idea or something with sentimental value, despite steady 2-3% yearly price increases I they're unlikely to cancel, and also unlikely to waste several hours moving a domain simply to save a few dollars a year. Godaddy's recent Q2 results show bookings are finally increasing (+5%) as a result of marketing spend, and Godaddy's new Airo tool (AI generated websites) provide a key alternative for small subset of customers who might want to "re-do" their website elsewhere using AI tools.

I think Godaddy is pretty inexpensive under 12x forward earnings with growth prospects, but I like the stock even more at $80, given the company heavily repurchases shares in the 90s. I've put 0.50% into the stock, and I also wrote several January $80 Strike Put options for $2.40, if the stock drops to $80 I will be happy to add another 0.50%. Godaddy at $210 last year was really indefensible, but I think at $105 with the share repurchase cannon at full blast, it's being valued like a software business in terminal decline, despite an extremely sticky customer base and new growth prospects. Goddady is unfortunately up pretty heavily today, hence the small sizing. Over the next several weeks I will build Godaddy into a 2-3% position, as long as it remains close to $100.
